status: Inventory of authored support; not a retrieval or answer score.

facts.claim: A custom component registered under a type name can be selected by a field using that name as its type.
conditions: The registration is available in the consuming form configuration.
limits: The pinned example uses NgModule FormlyModule.forRoot; setup style can vary by application.

facts.claim: A field key links its value to the model, while a string type selects a registered field type name.
limits: The example happens to use the same string for both; equality is not required.

facts.claim: The official password example uses its registered type name in a field configuration.
limits: The example uses an input-derived type; a consuming app must register its own name and component or inheritance.

facts.claim: Core FieldType exposes the field, model, form, options, props, and formControl.
A component class alone does not make its type name available; the application must register it under types.
Type registration supports component, extends, defaultOptions, and wrappers.
The configuration service fills missing field values through reverse deep merging of type defaults.
limits: A partial props object need not replace every inherited default; complex precedence should be checked against getMergedField.

facts.claim: The official password example extends input and sets defaults instead of reimplementing its renderer.
limits: This is an example pattern, not a guarantee about every custom type.

facts.claim: FieldWrapper exposes a fieldComponent insertion target for the wrapped field.
A wrapper decorates a field; it does not replace a missing control or value accessor.
Formly applies a configured defaultValue when a keyed field value is undefined.
conditions: The field is not hidden during the relevant build conditions.
limits: Array and JSON Schema defaults have additional behavior outside this claim.

facts.claim: A configured defaultValue does not universally replace an already defined model value.
limits: Null, false, and zero are defined values.

facts.claim: options.updateInitialValue() records a cloned reset baseline.
options.resetModel() restores the saved baseline or an explicitly supplied model, rebuilds the fields, and resets controls.
limits: Do not assume raw form.reset() is equivalent.

facts.claim: The modern expressions map supports a hide expression.
The modern expressions map supports a props.disabled expression.
A modern expressions function callback receives the field.
limits: Read field.model in its actual model scope rather than assuming it is the root model.

facts.claim: Legacy expressionProperties and hideExpression functions receive model, formState, and optionally field arguments.
Use field hide for constant visibility and a supported expression for conditional visibility.
limits: Arbitrary boolean entries are not established as a general expressions API.

facts.claim: The expression evaluator combines ancestor disabled state with a props.disabled expression, but not with a templateOptions.disabled expression.
conditions: The field has an ancestor whose disabled state is relevant.
limits: Both target paths can still update a disabled control.

facts.claim: In v6.3.12, expression paths props.disabled and templateOptions.disabled are not behaviorally interchangeable under ancestor disabled state.
conditions: A disabled ancestor affects the field's expression evaluation.
limits: Both paths update disabled controls; a mechanical rename can change behavior.

facts.claim: The default checkExpressionOn setting is modelChange.
limits: Formly v6.3.12 also observes formState changes in the form component.

facts.claim: options.checkExpressions(field) evaluates expressions, while options.detectChanges(field) invokes expression checks and marks relevant components.
An Observable returned from a supported onInit hook is subscribed to and disposed by the field component.
A manually created subscription inside a hook is not automatically the managed returned subscription.
limits: Provide corresponding cleanup for a manual subscription.

facts.claim: The default Formly registry enables lazy rendering.
The default Formly registry enables reset-on-hide.
The expression extension unregisters a hidden field control.
conditions: The relevant associated fields are hidden.

facts.claim: Reset-on-hide can remove a hidden field value from the model.
conditions: Reset-on-hide is active for the field.
The control is being unregistered after the relevant associated fields are hidden.

facts.claim: Showing a hidden keyed field re-registers its control.
conditions: The field has a keyed form control.

facts.claim: Setting resetOnHide to false skips the hide handler's value-clearing branch.
conditions: The field is hidden and its control is unregistered.
limits: The hidden control may still leave the active control tree.

facts.claim: Hiding one field that shares a key does not necessarily remove the shared control.
conditions: Other fields share that key or control.

facts.claim: Reset-on-hide can clear the child fields of a hidden FormArray.
conditions: Reset-on-hide is active for the field.
The hidden field has a FormArray control and child field group.

facts.claim: Showing a hidden field may reapply its configured defaultValue.
conditions: A defaultValue exists and the current field value is undefined.
limits: Showing a field does not unconditionally overwrite its current value.

facts.claim: For an application-computed initial value available before field build, initialize the model; the official demo prefers model initialization.
conditions: The initial value is available before the relevant field build.
limits: The demo does not prescribe a hook or an asynchronous update strategy.

facts.claim: A field defaultValue fills an undefined keyed model value when the field is eligible; it does not overwrite an already supplied model value.
limits: Hidden fields have separate build conditions.

facts.claim: A qualifying changed model input can trigger a FormlyForm rebuild.
conditions: The changed input passes the component change condition.
limits: This does not show that defaultValue reacts to arbitrary later state changes or that a field hook is required.

facts.claim: Material's form-field wrapper owns mat-form-field.
A plain core FieldType does not automatically provide Material's MatFormFieldControl integration.
limits: A custom Material control must account for the actual Material integration contract.

facts.claim: options.formState carries shared form context.
The generic parameter of FormlyFieldConfig<Props> describes props, not the model's key schema.
A Formly field key can be a string, number, or path array.
The default Formly props type permits additional properties.
limits: TypeScript accepting an extra prop does not prove a Material component consumes it.

facts.claim: Formly v6 core aliases templateOptions to props.
A field's type string resolves through registered types.
A registered type can contribute defaults, inheritance, and wrappers.
